questions.prompt: Which visited neighbor indicates a cycle in an undirected DFS?

choices.label: A visited neighbor other than the current node's parent.
choices.feedback: The edge back to the parent is the same undirected edge used to arrive, not a new cycle.

choices.label: Only a neighbor with a smaller numeric label.
choices.feedback: The edge back to the parent is the same undirected edge used to arrive, not a new cycle.

choices.label: Any visited neighbor, including the parent.
choices.feedback: The edge back to the parent is the same undirected edge used to arrive, not a new cycle.

questions.prompt: What else must hold after a cycle-free traversal?

choices.label: Every vertex was reached.
choices.feedback: A tree must be connected as well as acyclic; disconnected vertices fail that requirement.

choices.label: Every vertex has at most two neighbors.
choices.feedback: A tree must be connected as well as acyclic; disconnected vertices fail that requirement.

choices.label: The starting vertex has no parent.
choices.feedback: A tree must be connected as well as acyclic; disconnected vertices fail that requirement.
